markUrl.description: URL del monograma, usado como ícono de pestaña.

StoreLogoSpec.title: StoreLogoSpec
StoreLogoSpec.description:
The two marks a store shows instead of its plain name — TAL-11.

Independent halves: a brand may have a full wordmark and no
standalone mark. Only what is given travels, so a store with one of
the two is not treated as a store with none.

Per the user's decision of 2026-08-17 these are URLs, not uploads:
at provisioning time the tenant does not exist yet, so it has no
storage of its own to receive a file. Which hosts are acceptable is
the facade's call — it is the only side that knows its own storage —
so this side checks the scheme and stops there rather than keeping a
second host list that would drift from the first.

StoreNavLinkSpec.title: StoreNavLinkSpec
StoreNavLinkSpec.description:
One entry of the store's menu, as the dashboard sends it.

``href`` is checked against the same two shapes the store itself
accepts — a path on the store, or an absolute ``https`` URL — and
everything else is refused rather than corrected. A
protocol-relative ``//host`` is rejected EXPLICITLY: it starts with a
slash, so a check that only asked "is this a path" would wave through
a link to somebody else's origin.

surface.title: Surface

accent.title: Accent

accentSoft.description: Acento suave: degradados, bordes y estados hover.

textMuted.title: Textmuted

support.description: Acento NO textual (insignias). Se mide contra el umbral de componente, no el de texto.

StorePaletteSpec.title: StorePaletteSpec
StorePaletteSpec.description:
The store's full colour system — TAL-11, mirror of the facade's own.

All eight required when the block is present, and the block itself
optional. That asymmetry is the store facade's rule, not a choice
made here: a palette with four of eight keys leaves its contrast gate
measuring against a colour nobody supplied — blind for exactly the
tenant that configured it. Declaring the same shape on this side is
what turns that into a 422 the operator sees while filling the form,
instead of a 422 the provisioning job hits after the site exists.

camelCase on the wire for the two compound names, exactly as the
facade spells them. Renaming at either end adds a hop where a value
is dropped and nothing fails.

preset.description: Storefront design preset applied at creation

accentHex.title: Accenthex
accentHex.description: Brand accent as a 6-digit hex colour (e.g. #DE3340)

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: ISO 4217 code the store charges in. Validated against the workspace's currency catalogue when the job is created; omitted keeps today's default (the catalogue's first entry).

region.title: Region
region.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region composed into the store's locale — `es` + `GT` → `es-GT` — so `Intl` formats money the way the country expects. Omitted keeps today's behaviour: the bare language code, with no region.

palette.description: Paleta completa de la marca, 8 colores. Omitida, la tienda se pinta con las superficies derivadas del preset, como hoy.

logo.description: Logotipo y monograma de la tienda. Omitido, el encabezado muestra el nombre en texto, como hoy.

chrome.description: Menú de navegación de la tienda. Omitido, la tienda se sirve sin menú propio, como hoy.

legalPages.description: Términos y política de privacidad de la tienda. Omitidos, la tienda sirve el borrador por defecto con su propia marca.

StorefrontSpec.title: StorefrontSpec
StorefrontSpec.description:
The look a store is born with — TBC-04.

Optional on the job (``None`` for every job that is not a store, and for
a store whose creator expressed no preference), so no existing document
changes shape and the provisioning body stays exactly the one that ships
today when nobody chooses.

``accentHex`` is REJECTED, never sanitised: this value is the one thing
in the theme that reaches the storefront's DOM inside a ``<style>``, so a
permissive pattern is an injection surface, and a silently-corrected
colour is a shop that does not look like what its owner picked.

The field is spelled in camelCase on purpose. It is the wire name the
store's facade takes, and the same name the dashboard sends; renaming it
at either end of the chain would add a hop where a value can be dropped
without anything failing — which is the exact defect this story exists to
close. ``TokenRequest.apiKey`` is the same call in this repo.

SubscriptionInvitationCreateRequest.title: SubscriptionInvitationCreateRequest
SubscriptionInvitationCreateRequest.description:
Body for issuing an invitation.

``customer_id`` is REQUIRED, and that is the whole of D-21: an invitation is
for one named customer and one use. There is deliberately no "anonymous
invitation" shape, because a link two people can open produces one shared
checkout, one charge id, and a second payer with no record of their charge.

No amount: it is the plan's.

SubscriptionPlanCreateRequest.title: SubscriptionPlanCreateRequest
SubscriptionPlanCreateRequest.description: Create body. NO ``currency``: it is derived from the business (D-15).

SubscriptionPlanUpdateRequest.title: SubscriptionPlanUpdateRequest
SubscriptionPlanUpdateRequest.description:
Patch body.

``amount`` and ``interval_days`` are accepted by the SCHEMA and refused by
the SERVICE once the plan is published (D-20), with a message that says to
archive and create another. Rejecting them here instead would answer a bare
422 with no code the dashboard could translate into that instruction — and
they are perfectly legal on a draft.

Omitted vs explicit null are distinguished via ``model_fields_set``, so a
description CAN be cleared and a field nobody mentioned is never touched.

TaskWithSubtasksResponse.title: TaskWithSubtasksResponse
TaskWithSubtasksResponse.description:
`GET /tasks/{id}/subtasks` (RF-5) — the task alongside its subtasks.

`GET /tasks/{id}/subtasks`'s access rule is BROADER than any
`GET /tasks?scope=` (creator, assignee, task_manager, OR anyone holding
the skill of at least one subtask, TSK-03's 3rd scenario) — a caller who
reaches a task ONLY through skill-match may have no other way to fetch
its title/status, since it will not appear in their own `GET /tasks`
list under any scope. Embedding the task here means `TaskDetailPage`
does not need a second, narrower-scoped request that could 404 for
exactly the caller this endpoint exists to serve.

TenantUserDirectoryItem.title: TenantUserDirectoryItem
TenantUserDirectoryItem.description:
D-14, extended: `OwnerRef` (`user_id`, `email`) plus the user's
CURRENT `skill_ids`.

Without this the assignment picker (`UserSkillsModal`) would have no way
to pre-check a user's existing skills before `PATCH /skills/users/{id}`
— which REPLACES the set wholesale, so opening the modal and saving
would silently wipe every skill the user already had. Extending the
directory response (rather than adding a second `GET
/skills/users/{id}` endpoint) keeps the picker to the one request it
already makes to populate itself.

TerminalRequestCreate.title: TerminalRequestCreate
TerminalRequestCreate.description:
Body of the create call.

``extra="forbid"``: the tax id, the legal name and the TRADING name are
DERIVED from the Business and its branch server-side, so sending them is not
merely ignored — it is refused, which is what stops an application being
filed under someone else's identity and what makes that refusal visible
instead of silent.

``commercial_name`` used to be an optional free-text field here, and it was
the one detail the merchant had to type despite the server already holding
it: the trading name IS the branch's name. Asking for it invited a value
that disagreed with the branch it was filed against, with nothing to
reconcile the two.

TerminalRequestPatch.title: TerminalRequestPatch
TerminalRequestPatch.description:
Partial update of the applicant, while the request is still editable.

Every field is optional, and an omitted field is distinguished from an
explicit ``null`` by ``model_fields_set`` at the service layer: without that
distinction a client could never tell "leave this alone" from "clear this",
and clearing a required field would be a 422 the merchant cannot act on.

'You' : 'Team'`, which made every automatic message in a manual-review thread render as if the owner had written it himself. Measured live in verify-epic-e2e 2026-08-17 on the review ticket the sweep opened. Additive and defaulted to `user`, so every message written before this reads exactly as it did and no backfill is needed.

TradingConfigPatch.title: TradingConfigPatch
TradingConfigPatch.description:
Typed override of the trading namespace for ONE tenant.

Every field is optional and `null` CLEARS the override (falling back to the
platform default), which is why the handler distinguishes "omitted" from
"explicitly null" via `model_fields_set` — without that distinction a
tenant's override could never be removed, only overwritten.

`provider` is validated against the factory's own list rather than a second
copy of it: two lists are one list plus a way for them to disagree.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Transaction amount in merchant's configured currency (must be positive)

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Which of YOUR OWN balances to top up (MCB-08). Omit to use your primary billing — the previous behaviour — or send `branch_id` instead to charge in a commerce's own currency. The server resolves the billing from (your user, this currency), so this names a currency and never a billing id: you cannot address someone else's balance even by guessing an id, because none is accepted here.

branch_id.title: Branch Id
branch_id.description:
The BRANCH this charge belongs to. Send it whenever the money being collected is a commerce's — a subscription, an invoice, an order — and the charge is issued in **that commerce's currency**, not in the payer's primary one.

A branch, not a commerce, because the branch is the unit the rest of this API already speaks: an invoice certifies under ITS establishment code (`CreateInvoiceRequest.branchId`), and a commerce with more than one coded branch REFUSES to guess which one issued — so an integration that emits invoices is already holding a branch id. The commerce, and therefore the currency, is derived from it server-side.

Without it the currency comes from your primary balance, which is wrong as soon as one account owns commerces in different currencies: a commerce trading in quetzales was charged in dollars because its owner's primary balance happened to be USD.

You must be authorised for the branch's commerce (404 if the branch is unknown or its commerce is not yours, 403 if your role cannot take payments) and hold a balance in that commerce's currency (404 naming the currency otherwise). The settlement balance is derived server-side — it is never named by this request, because where the money lands is not the caller's decision.

Sending `currency` alongside this is allowed only when the two agree; a disagreement is refused with `400` instead of one of them being silently dropped.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Additional metadata — echoed back in the outbound webhook payload

merchant_reference.title: Merchant Reference
merchant_reference.description: Free-form identifier the merchant attaches to the transaction. Echoed back unchanged in the outbound webhook payload — use it to correlate the webhook with your local order without parsing metadata.

return_url.title: Return Url
return_url.description:
Where the payer's BROWSER lands once checkout finishes — approved or not. Without it the payer stops on the payment page, on a domain that is not yours, with no way back.

Must be HTTPS and its host must be registered for this App via `POST /webhooks/config/domains` (the same allowlist the outbound webhooks use; DNS verification is NOT required).

Two variables are substituted into it, URL-encoded: `{{transaction_id}}` and `{{merchant_reference}}` — the transaction id does not exist yet when you send this, so a return page that needs it has no other way to receive it.

It is a REDIRECT, not a notification: the payer can close the tab before it happens. The webhook remains the only thing that settles an order.

customer_email.title: Customer Email
customer_email.description:
Your BUYER's email address. When the payment is approved, 1Platform emails them a receipt for it; the payment provider does not send anything to the buyer.

Optional — omit it and nothing changes. It is never echoed back by this or any other endpoint.

The address must be a well-formed mailbox (RFC 5321 caps it at 254 characters); anything else is refused with `400` before the payment provider is contacted, so a typo costs you nothing.

Do NOT use `metadata.userId` for this: that value is forwarded to the payment provider as the payer identifier and is not a receipt address.

The receipt is a courtesy to the buyer, not a settlement signal — the webhook remains the only thing that settles an order.

UpdateBranchRequest.title: UpdateBranchRequest
UpdateBranchRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /businesses/{businessId}/branches/{branchId}``.

Three independent patchable concerns, all optional: the display ``name``,
the pickup block (deliveries) and the FEL establishment code (fiscal
identity, EST-01/D-4). A request must carry at least one —
``extra="forbid"`` keeps a typo (or an attempt to rewrite ``commerceId``)
a loud 422 instead of a silent no-op, but it does NOT reject an empty body,
and it does NOT reject an explicit ``null`` on a known optional field. Both
of those are handled below.

``name`` is added by fel-sincronizar-establecimientos (SES-02). Until then a
branch could be named ONCE, at creation, and never again: this DTO had no
``name`` field and ``extra="forbid"`` rejected it, so `Branch.name` had
exactly one writer in the whole codebase. That made the establishment sync
unshippable as approved — the sync OVERWRITES the name the business typed
with the one the registry declares, and the user approved that overwrite on
the stated premise that they could "rename the branch again whenever they
want" (requerimiento P-2, and an acceptance criterion of SES-02). Without a
write path that premise was false and the overwrite was irreversible.

This is the display label only. It is NOT the fiscal identity: that lives in
``establishment_code`` and in the registry's own ``fel_commercial_name`` /
``fel_address``, which the sync keeps separately and which this endpoint
cannot touch. Contrast ``BusinessService.LOCKED_FIELDS``, which freezes a
*business* name and address once registered with the tax authority — those
ARE the fiscal identity, a branch's display name is not.

``establishment_code`` is declared ``strict`` on purpose: Pydantic's lax
mode would coerce the string ``"2"`` into ``2`` and we would forward it
happily, but the emitter's contract requires a JSON **number** and answers
400 to a string. Failing here makes that a 422 the caller can act on,
instead of a 400 three layers down whose message we do not own.

defaultBranchId.title: Defaultbranchid
defaultBranchId.description: Branch that issues invoices created without `branchId` (EST-06). Must be a branch of THIS business. Unlike every other field here, an explicit `null` CLEARS the designation instead of meaning 'leave unchanged' — the field is nullable by design (the other three back required columns, where null would brick the row), so 'no default branch' has to be expressible or the merchant could designate one and never take it back. Omit the key to leave it untouched.

UpdateBusinessRequest.title: UpdateBusinessRequest
UpdateBusinessRequest.description:
Partial update of a business. Fiscal identity is immutable.

`documentNumber` / `documentType` are absent BY CONTRACT: invoices were
already certified against that NIT with the FEL provider, so changing it
would desynchronise them. `extra="forbid"` is what turns "absent from the
schema" into an actual 422 — Pydantic's default silently ignores unknown
keys, which would answer 200 while quietly dropping the change.

WhatsAppConfigPatchRequest.description:

give two lists that drift.

WhatsAppEvent.title: WhatsAppEvent
WhatsAppEvent.description:
The four notification sites of the dedicated host (D-14).

Four, not one: the previous shape sized the enum for the disk threshold and
left the other three sites talking only to the old channel. ``disk_alert``
covers both severity levels — the level is a parameter, not an event,
because the spacing window is per level and lives in the caller.

WhatsAppKeys.title: WhatsAppKeys
WhatsAppKeys.description:
Per-App outbound WhatsApp credential (Fernet-encrypted).

Clone of :class:`AdsKeys`, and the credential CHAIN is the same: this
per-tenant override first, the platform default
(``PlatformSettings.whatsapp.credentials_encrypted``) second — so rotating
the common credential is one document, not N.

What is deliberately NOT cloned is the *shape* of the ads secret.
``AdsKeys.credential_encrypted`` holds a composite ``app_id|app_secret``
because that provider's OAuth dance needs a confidential client. This one
holds **a single opaque long-lived system token**: the advertising
credential is a different kind of token and its scopes
(``ads_management``, ``pages_show_list``, ``business_management``) do not
imply messaging, so reusing it was never a design option — it does not
work.

Written ONLY by the platform
(``PATCH /platform/apps/{app_id}/keys/whatsapp``), never by the tenant:
``whatsapp`` is in ``_PROTECTED_CONFIG_KEYS``, because the beneficiary of a
safeguard cannot be the one who writes it.

``phone_number_id`` is the provider's numeric ASSET id for the sending
number — not the number in readable form. It is not a secret, which is why
it sits beside the credential rather than inside it and is safe to return
in the boolean-plus-metadata response.

WhatsAppKeysUpdateRequest.title: WhatsAppKeysUpdateRequest
WhatsAppKeysUpdateRequest.description:
The tenant's messaging credential. `null` clears it (falls back to platform).

The field is named **`credential`** and that is load-bearing, not a style
choice: `"credential"` is in `_REDACTED_KEYS`, which is the only thing that
keeps this body out of `ApiLog` — where it would sit for 90 days and be
re-served through `GET /api/v1/logs`. Renaming it to `api_token` or `wa_token`
silently removes that redaction, so any rename needs the new line in
`_REDACTED_KEYS` in the SAME commit.

Being able to OMIT it is what makes the channel switchable off without
re-sending the secret.

WhatsAppPlatformConfigPatchRequest.title: WhatsAppPlatformConfigPatchRequest
WhatsAppPlatformConfigPatchRequest.description:
Sparse patch over the PLATFORM `whatsapp` namespace.

This is the endpoint that loads the DESTINATION of the operations alerts.
Without it, `ops_recipients` could only be set by committing the team's phone
numbers to the repository or editing the database by hand.

`credentials_encrypted` is refused here even though it lives in this
namespace: the credential has its own endpoint whose field name is what
redacts it from the API log, and nested under `values` that redaction does
not apply.

WorkspaceLimitRow.title: WorkspaceLimitRow
WorkspaceLimitRow.description:
One ceiling, and where the server applies it.

``limit`` is ``null`` when no ceiling is declared. It is never ``0`` for
that case: a console cannot tell "no ceiling" from "a ceiling of zero" if
both arrive as a number, and it would paint a full bar over an unlimited
resource (PAD-14 CA-3).

``limit``/``used``/``remaining`` are decimal STRINGS because the same row
shape carries counts and money, and a money ceiling that travels as a JSON
number arrives rounded by the reader's float parser.

tags.description: Create user accounts and obtain user JWT tokens. New users are automatically set up with billing and a subscription plan.

tags.name: My Profile
tags.description: View the authenticated user's profile information (username, email, status).

tags.name: Balance & Billing
tags.description: Check your current balance, currency, and active subscription details.

tags.name: Content Categories
tags.description: Browse available categories used to classify websites and generated content.

tags.name: Websites
tags.description: Add, update, search, and delete websites for the authenticated user. Also generate legal pages (privacy policy, cookie policy, legal notice).

tags.name: Website Plugins
tags.description: The site's WordPress plugin inventory and the pull-channel orders (sync, activate, deactivate, delete, install) it picks up and applies. Ordering requires a dashboard session; only the site itself may claim and report on its own orders.

tags.name: Link Building & Search Console
tags.description: Register and verify websites in the link-building marketplace, and manage Google Search Console properties and sitemaps.

tags.name: AI Generators
tags.description: Generate AI content on demand: fictional comments for blogs, images from text prompts, and complete profile cards with bio and avatar.

tags.name: Payments
tags.description: Create payment transactions, get a checkout URL, and retrieve your full transaction history.

tags.name: Payment Links
tags.description: Emit shareable payment links so a business can charge an external customer who is not a 1Platform user. Merchant endpoints require the two-token auth; the `/pay/{token}` link itself is public — the token is the capability.

tags.name: Payment Terminals
tags.description: Apply for a card terminal so a business can accept cards in person, attach the required documents, track the application and receive the activation code. Merchant endpoints require the two-token auth; the app-store redirect is public because it discloses nothing.

tags.name: Deliveries
tags.description: Register, dispatch and track shipments for a business. Own-fleet mode works end to end with no third party; courier mode is a configurable dispatch seam. All endpoints require the two-token auth; writes additionally require a branch-admin role.

tags.name: Ads
tags.description: Advertising campaigns funded from the workspace balance. The merchant connects the brand their ads are published as, builds a simple campaign, adds budget from their balance, and gets back whatever was not spent when it closes. Funding requires an `Idempotency-Key`; the remainder is returned once the reported spend settles, not at the instant of closing. All endpoints require the two-token auth, and the vertical is switched on per workspace by platform staff.

tags.name: Subscriptions
tags.description: View subscription plan details and current plan status.

tags.name: Billing & Consumption
tags.description: Track credit consumption history and view usage summaries grouped by operation type.

tags.name: Payment Notifications
tags.description: Receive automatic payment status updates from the payment service. No authentication required — designed for server-to-server callbacks. All responses return HTTP 200 to prevent retries.

tags.name: Internal Webhooks
tags.description: Internal webhook endpoints for automated billing operations. Called by the payment webhook dispatcher after transaction status changes. Authenticated via internal bearer token — not for external use.

tags.name: Webhook Configuration
tags.description: Manage webhook configuration for your application: register, update, list, and delete the URLs that receive payment status callbacks.

tags.name: Businesses & Branches
tags.description: Register business entities and their branches for electronic invoicing. Each branch can issue invoices independently.

tags.name: Electronic Invoicing (FEL)
tags.description: Create, list, view, and cancel electronic invoices (FEL Guatemala). Invoices are linked to a business and emitted using its tax ID (NIT).

tags.name: Activity Logs
tags.description: View, filter, and clear API activity logs. Also ingest client-side log entries for centralized observability.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Analytics integration — connect, provision properties, track content performance, and query real-time metrics.

tags.name: AdSense
tags.description: AdSense integration — connect your account via OAuth, monitor site approval states, view earnings reports, and track policy compliance.

tags.name: Agents Catalog
tags.description: Browse the agent template catalog to discover pre-built automation recipes.

tags.name: Agents Tools
tags.description: Browse the tools an agent can be given: what each one does, whether it charges and how much, and whether this workspace can use it today. A tool that is unavailable is listed with its reason rather than hidden.

tags.name: Agents Wizard
tags.description: Create agents interactively using a guided wizard powered by AI. Start a session, answer questions, and confirm to deploy.

tags.name: Agents CRUD
tags.description: Create, list, read, update, and delete agent definitions.

tags.name: Agents Execution
tags.description: Trigger agent runs, list execution history, inspect run details, and stop running or pending executions.

tags.name: Agents Metrics
tags.description: View aggregated operational metrics for the agent platform (admin-level).

tags.name: Agents Actions
tags.description: List, inspect, and consume human-in-the-loop actions generated by agent runs. Actions require manual approval before the agent proceeds.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: Search, register, renew, and manage domains. Configure DNS records, nameservers, and WHOIS contacts. Domain costs are deducted from your 1Platform balance.

tags.name: Onboarding
tags.description: Guided onboarding flow for new users — start a session, complete the required steps, and convert it into an active account with billing initialized.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: Whitelabel dashboard bootstrap — per-app branding, theme, modules, layout, feature flags, and i18n bundles. Drives the SPA boot flow. Read endpoints return strong ETags for CDN / client caching.

tags.name: Dashboard Settings
tags.description: Per-app dashboard settings store — read, upsert, and delete free-form configuration entries scoped to your app (used by the SPA for feature flags, layout overrides, and tenant-specific preferences).

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: In-app notifications for the authenticated user — list, create, mark as read, and check the unread badge count.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Tasks — assign to a tenant user, decompose into sequential, skill-gated subtasks, and create programmatically via a ServiceKey (tasks-subtasks-skills).

tags.name: Subtasks
tags.description: A user's claimable/assigned subtasks across every task, and the claim/complete state transition (tasks-subtasks-skills).

tags.name: Skills
tags.description: Tenant skill catalogue and per-user skill assignment — gates who can create Tasks and claim skill-gated Subtasks (tasks-subtasks-skills).

tags.name: Support
tags.description: Customer support workspace — open and reply to tickets, browse frequently asked questions, and let admins curate the FAQ catalog.

tags.name: Referrals
tags.description: Referral program lookups — resolve a referral code to its public metadata (program name, signup URL, app branding).

tags.name: User Authentication
tags.description: Passwordless dashboard login — request a magic link, exchange it for an access + refresh token pair, rotate refresh tokens, and revoke sessions on logout.

tags.name: Platform Admin
tags.description: Cross-tenant administration for the 1Platform team — provision new apps, list every registered app, inspect a single app, and view platform-wide metrics. Requires the superadmin role.

tags.name: Tenant Admin
tags.description: Per-tenant administration scoped to the actor's `app_id`. Lets the tenant `app_admin` role list/manage users, roles and impersonation, plus read business, invoicing, billing, domain and operational data for their own tenant.

tags.name: Provisioning
tags.description: One-click asynchronous provisioning of new Atlas tenants (dashboard + app) for a domain. The `app_admin` role starts a job and polls its progress; every resource is scoped to the caller's own workspace (`app_id`), so a cross-tenant job id returns 404 without leaking its existence.

tags.name: API Developer
tags.description: A caller's own API credentials. Several may exist at once, each revocable on its own, and the secret is returned exactly once — at the moment it is issued. Only its SHA-256 is stored, so there is no endpoint that can show it again; a lost credential is replaced, not recovered. Disabling or deleting one cuts it off on the next request, including for a token already issued from it and still inside its expiry window.

tags.name: API Developer (admin)
tags.description: The tenant administrator's view of the same credentials: who holds what, when each was last exchanged, and the ability to cut any of them the moment one leaks. No response on this surface ever carries a secret — not by filtering, but because the only two endpoints that return one belong to the credential's owner. The workspace credential refuses being disabled or deleted: the front-ends carry it compiled into their bundle, so cutting it would sign every user of the tenant out at once. Rotating it is the supported path.

tags.name: Trading
tags.description:
1Trade: turn part of your balance into an automated position that buys at a market amount and sells at a higher one, optionally repeating and compounding the realised result.

Creating a trade RESERVES the amount; the balance only moves against a confirmed fill, and what comes back is the amount really received net of fees — never the theoretical target. The result is credited as 1Platform balance and is not withdrawable.

tags.name: Trading Agent
tags.description:
The surface a 1Trade monitor uses. Authenticated with a service credential alone (`Authorization: Bearer ak-svc-…`) carrying the `trade.execute` capability and platform scope — no app token and no user token.

The monitor decides **when** to look at a cycle. The server decides what, how much and whether: it derives the action from the cycle's own state, re-reads the price itself, and re-checks the trigger. The request body carries no action, no reason and no amount.

tags.name: Heatmaps
tags.description: Measure how visitors use a site: where they click and how far they scroll. A site installs capture by pasting one `<script>` tag; the collector is served by this API and does the rest. Samples are aggregated on write, so nothing raw is ever stored.

tags.name: Activation
tags.description:
Receives paid activation purchases from the storefront that sells the activation package.

**Not part of the two-token model.** The caller is another product and holds no 1Platform credentials, so the HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw request body is the credential (`X-Bowerbird-Signature` plus `X-Bowerbird-Timestamp`, which bounds replay).

Delivery is retried, so the endpoint is idempotent on `event_key`: a repeat answers 200 and changes nothing. The amount of balance a purchase is worth is resolved from the platform's package catalogue and never read from the request body.
